blocks.text: Odottaessa sat in the corpus's harshest review, unglossed: muutama vanhus oli siinä samalla, kuuntelin odottaessa. This is a second infinitive — a compact way to say 'while doing something' without needing a full kun-clause (Lesson 22). One word instead of a whole clause, just like Lesson 29's referative construction.

blocks.annotated: Kuuntelin {odottaessani|grammar|second infinitive + possessive suffix|while I waited}.

blocks.title: Eavesdropping, grammatically compressed
blocks.text: In the original review, kuuntelin odottaessa lets the reviewer casually mention they were listening in on other customers' conversations while they themselves waited — all folded into a single compact verb form. It's a small, efficient aside, exactly the kind of detail that makes a complaint feel like an eyewitness account rather than hearsay.

blocks.content: Take a verb stem and add {-essa|grammar|second infinitive suffix|while doing} or -essä to mean 'while/when doing [that action]'. Odottaa (to wait) → {odottaessa|grammar|second infinitive|while waiting}. This single word replaces an entire kun-clause: kun odotin becomes odottaessani — same meaning, more compact.

items.en: While driving, the car began to shake.

blocks.text: Piece 2 — Adding the possessive suffix for 'while I...'

blocks.title: Lesson 14's suffixes, once again
blocks.text: To say specifically 'while I was waiting' rather than a general 'while waiting', attach Lesson 14's possessive suffix: odottaessa + -ni → {odottaessani|grammar|second infinitive + possessive suffix|while I was waiting}. Same suffix family as autoni, paikkansa, and tehneensä — always marking whose action or thing is being described.

items.fi: Kuuntelin {odottaessani|grammar|second infinitive + possessive suffix, 1st person|while I was waiting}.
items.en: I listened while I was waiting.

items.fi: He riitelivät {puhuessaan|grammar|second infinitive + possessive suffix, 3rd person|while they were talking}.
items.en: They argued while they were talking.

blocks.text: Piece 3 — A compact family, like Lesson 29's

blocks.content: You now have two ways to build 'while/when' sentences: the plain kun-clause (Lesson 22) and this compact second-infinitive shape. Formal written Finnish — again, the register of these reviews — often prefers the compact version, exactly as with Lesson 29's referative construction. Recognition matters more than fluent production here too.

items.fi: {Odottaessani|grammar|second infinitive + possessive suffix|while I was waiting} kuuntelin.
items.en: While I was waiting, I listened.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: What did you hear while you were waiting?

lines.speaker: B
lines.fi: Kuuntelin, ja kuulin korkeita hintoja perusteltavan muille asiakkaille.
lines.en: I listened, and I heard high prices being justified to other customers.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: While driving home, did the car work well?

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: No. It started shaking already on the way.

blocks.title: Paul Noble Rule
blocks.text: Same advice as Lesson 29: reach for the plain kun-clause when writing yourself, and simply recognise -essa/-essä plus a possessive suffix when you meet it in a review. You now have two matching compact constructions in your toolkit — one for reported actions (tehneensä), one for simultaneous timing (odottaessani).

blocks.content: Odottaessani: O-dot-ta-es-sa-ni (six syllables — long, but broken into odot-ta-essa-ni it settles). Ajaessa: A-ja-es-sa (four syllables, the 'j' is a 'y' sound). Puhuessaan: PU-hu-es-saan (long final 'aan').
